purpose: Hard denominator for the repository claim that Davis--Kahan 1970 is 100% formalized.

selection_definition.counts_as_result: Exactly the four unnumbered Section 2 headline theorems and every named theorem, proposition, lemma, and corollary that Davis--Kahan actually establish in this paper.
selection_definition.statement_boundary: Only hypotheses, conclusions, and scope that belong to the printed result statement count. Setup, proof steps, examples, immediate consequences, and incidental later remarks remain source-fidelity material. A later source passage affects a counted result ONLY when it is necessary to determine what Davis and Kahan actually claim in that result under the paper's own semantics -- a standing convention, a definition, or a scope sentence the printed statement relies on. It does NOT enlarge the result merely because it discusses a stronger variant, an extension, a consequence, or another case. If such a passage is itself a distinct substantive result that Davis and Kahan introduce AND prove, it belongs in the denominator, and that is a decision for a fresh result-selection audit, not something the atom ledger may do on its own. CORRECTED 2026-08-31: this field previously ended "A later source passage that explicitly extends the proved scope of a counted result is part of that result's scope and must be covered", which contradicted `does_not_count`'s own entry for scope remarks outside the printed result environment and would have let the atom ledger enlarge the denominator by reclassification.
does_not_count: sharpness or interpretation commentary outside a designated result
immediate consequences or scope remarks outside the printed result environment
Section 10 open questions and their motivating special cases
claims explicitly left unresolved or whose proof is deferred to an open question
later proof-section restatements of a result already counted at its source statement
selection_definition.false_printed_result_policy: A designated result that is false remains in the denominator and is completed by exact formal refutation plus the repository best-effort repair obligation.

formalization_criterion.unit: The fundamental unit is a Davis--Kahan RESULT, not a source atom. Source-fidelity atoms exist so a hostile reviewer can audit the source-to-Lean correspondence; they do not independently create proof obligations.
formalization_criterion.membership: A source item belongs to the formalization denominator when Davis and Kahan present it as a mathematical result of the paper AND provide a proof for it. This is the four unnumbered Section 2 headline theorems plus the paper's proved named theorems, propositions, lemmas and corollaries. A fresh source audit may identify another genuinely independent proved result; definitions, proof steps, intermediate identities, examples, explanatory remarks, immediate consequences, restatements, and open or deferred claims do not become separate obligations merely because they contain mathematical assertions.
formalization_criterion.objective: Semantic equivalence of RESULTS, not reproduction of the paper's proofs. The Lean proof may use different lemmas, abstractions, representations, reductions, proof order, or stronger intermediate results. An intermediate step of the paper need not be separately formalized unless it is itself a counted result.
formalization_criterion.hostile_review_claim: For every counted result the repository must identify canonical Lean theorem evidence and support this claim: the hypotheses, mathematical objects, scope and conclusions of this Lean theorem are the same as those of the corresponding Davis--Kahan result, after making explicit any definitions or standing conventions the paper uses.
hostile_review_checklist: the precise angle, subspace, residual, perturbation or operator being bounded
real versus complex scalar scope where applicable
spectral-gap assumptions, including any half-infinite cases actually belonging to the result
standing assumptions or nonlocal conventions genuinely required by the paper
representative or multiplicity issues that affect unitarily invariant norms
formalization_criterion.equivalence_lemmas: Where a source formulation and the Lean formulation are equivalent but the equivalence is not apparent from the theorem types, an explicit correspondence lemma must be supplied.
formalization_criterion.terminal_certificate: Every substantive result introduced and proved by Davis and Kahan has canonical Lean evidence -- a proof, or an exact formal refutation where the printed result is false -- and every canonical Lean statement has been audited against the corresponding source result closely enough to withstand a hostile theorem-by-theorem comparison.
formalization_criterion.atoms_are_evidence_not_obligations: The source-atom inventory is deliberately far larger than the denominator. It is the evidence base for auditing the counted results, and a scope atom that records an extension, variant, consequence or another case is fidelity material, classified `result_adjacent_extension`.

results.norm_class_reading:
The printed quantifier is "every normalized unitary-invariant norm" as Section 1 defines it: the norm axioms, ||VKW|| = ||K|| for unitary V and W (1.9), ||uv*|| = ||u|| ||v|| on rank one, left/right multiplication by a contraction does not increase the norm, and -- stated in the same passage, at (1.11)-(1.13) -- Fan dominance in the strong form, "||K|| <= ||L|| for every unitary-invariant norm iff the inequality holds for every Ky Fan norm".

Two Lean objects model that class here, and NEITHER is the printed class as a type. `SymmetricNormingFunction` is the Gohberg--Krein reading: a dimension-coherent normalized symmetric gauge, read on the complete approximation-singular-value sequence as the supremum of its finite prefixes.  In finite dimension that is every unitarily invariant norm; in infinite dimension it is not, and the hostile follow-up review of 2026-09-05 named the witness -- `T |-> ||T|| + ||pi(T)||` with `pi` the Calkin quotient map is unitarily invariant, normalized on rank one, contraction-monotone and Fan dominant, but agrees with the operator norm on every finite-rank operator, so no symmetric gauge generates it.  `KyFanDominantIdealFamily` is the axiomatic reading -- a complete symmetric operator ideal family with Fan dominance as a field -- and it does contain that norm.

The estimates do not distinguish them, and that is now a theorem rather than a remark.  `symmetricNorming_of_kyFanDominant` sends an estimate proved at every Fan-dominant family to every symmetric norming function; `kyFanDominant_of_symmetricNorming` is the converse, obtained by instantiating at `kyFanNormingFunction k`, the Ky Fan gauge presented as a coherent symmetric norming function, whose ideal contains every bounded operator; and `symmetricNorming_iff_kyFanDominant` states the equivalence.  Both quantifiers are therefore equivalent to weak Ky Fan majorization, which is exactly the criterion the source announces it will use.  A row certified on a `SymmetricNormingFunction` endpoint consequently delivers the printed scope, including at unitarily invariant norms outside the symmetrically normed ideals; the transport is registered on the row rather than left as an appeal to what a reviewer should already know.

results.norm_class_reading:
The printed quantifier is "every normalized unitary-invariant norm" as Section 1 defines it: the norm axioms, ||VKW|| = ||K|| for unitary V and W (1.9), ||uv*|| = ||u|| ||v|| on rank one, left/right multiplication by a contraction does not increase the norm, and -- stated in the same passage, at (1.11)-(1.13) -- Fan dominance in the strong form, "||K|| <= ||L|| for every unitary-invariant norm iff the inequality holds for every Ky Fan norm".

Two Lean objects model that class here, and NEITHER is the printed class as a type. `SymmetricNormingFunction` is the Gohberg--Krein reading: a dimension-coherent normalized symmetric gauge, read on the complete approximation-singular-value sequence as the supremum of its finite prefixes.  In finite dimension that is every unitarily invariant norm; in infinite dimension it is not, and the hostile follow-up review of 2026-09-05 named the witness -- `T |-> ||T|| + ||pi(T)||` with `pi` the Calkin quotient map is unitarily invariant, normalized on rank one, contraction-monotone and Fan dominant, but agrees with the operator norm on every finite-rank operator, so no symmetric gauge generates it.  `KyFanDominantIdealFamily` is the axiomatic reading -- a complete symmetric operator ideal family with Fan dominance as a field -- and it does contain that norm.

The estimates do not distinguish them, and that is now a theorem rather than a remark.  `symmetricNorming_of_kyFanDominant` sends an estimate proved at every Fan-dominant family to every symmetric norming function; `kyFanDominant_of_symmetricNorming` is the converse, obtained by instantiating at `kyFanNormingFunction k`, the Ky Fan gauge presented as a coherent symmetric norming function, whose ideal contains every bounded operator; and `symmetricNorming_iff_kyFanDominant` states the equivalence.  Both quantifiers are therefore equivalent to weak Ky Fan majorization, which is exactly the criterion the source announces it will use.  A row certified on a `SymmetricNormingFunction` endpoint consequently delivers the printed scope, including at unitarily invariant norms outside the symmetrically normed ideals; the transport is registered on the row rather than left as an appeal to what a reviewer should already know.

results.norm_class_reading:
The printed quantifier is "every normalized unitary-invariant norm" as Section 1 defines it: the norm axioms, ||VKW|| = ||K|| for unitary V and W (1.9), ||uv*|| = ||u|| ||v|| on rank one, left/right multiplication by a contraction does not increase the norm, and -- stated in the same passage, at (1.11)-(1.13) -- Fan dominance in the strong form, "||K|| <= ||L|| for every unitary-invariant norm iff the inequality holds for every Ky Fan norm".

Two Lean objects model that class here, and NEITHER is the printed class as a type. `SymmetricNormingFunction` is the Gohberg--Krein reading: a dimension-coherent normalized symmetric gauge, read on the complete approximation-singular-value sequence as the supremum of its finite prefixes.  In finite dimension that is every unitarily invariant norm; in infinite dimension it is not, and the hostile follow-up review of 2026-09-05 named the witness -- `T |-> ||T|| + ||pi(T)||` with `pi` the Calkin quotient map is unitarily invariant, normalized on rank one, contraction-monotone and Fan dominant, but agrees with the operator norm on every finite-rank operator, so no symmetric gauge generates it.  `KyFanDominantIdealFamily` is the axiomatic reading -- a complete symmetric operator ideal family with Fan dominance as a field -- and it does contain that norm.

The estimates do not distinguish them, and that is now a theorem rather than a remark.  `symmetricNorming_of_kyFanDominant` sends an estimate proved at every Fan-dominant family to every symmetric norming function; `kyFanDominant_of_symmetricNorming` is the converse, obtained by instantiating at `kyFanNormingFunction k`, the Ky Fan gauge presented as a coherent symmetric norming function, whose ideal contains every bounded operator; and `symmetricNorming_iff_kyFanDominant` states the equivalence.  Both quantifiers are therefore equivalent to weak Ky Fan majorization, which is exactly the criterion the source announces it will use.  A row certified on a `SymmetricNormingFunction` endpoint consequently delivers the printed scope, including at unitarily invariant norms outside the symmetrically normed ideals; the transport is registered on the row rather than left as an appeal to what a reviewer should already know.

results.norm_class_reading:
The printed quantifier is "every normalized unitary-invariant norm" as Section 1 defines it: the norm axioms, ||VKW|| = ||K|| for unitary V and W (1.9), ||uv*|| = ||u|| ||v|| on rank one, left/right multiplication by a contraction does not increase the norm, and -- stated in the same passage, at (1.11)-(1.13) -- Fan dominance in the strong form, "||K|| <= ||L|| for every unitary-invariant norm iff the inequality holds for every Ky Fan norm".

Two Lean objects model that class here, and NEITHER is the printed class as a type. `SymmetricNormingFunction` is the Gohberg--Krein reading: a dimension-coherent normalized symmetric gauge, read on the complete approximation-singular-value sequence as the supremum of its finite prefixes. nonlocal_source_interpretation.accepted_reading: Section 8 is printed at the paper's MAIN BOUNDED SETTING, and the phrase "the hypotheses of the tan 2theta theorem" imports the tan 2theta theorem as the main body states it.  Three things in the source of record support this.  First, Section 1 fixes the default explicitly: "In the main bounded setting A = A* and A + H = (A + H)* are bounded.  The paper ALSO allows self-adjoint unbounded A when the later domain conditions are met" -- bounded is the setting, unbounded is an allowance.  Second, the Section 2 scope paragraph attaches that allowance to a named list: "The paper states THE FOUR MAIN RESULTS for infinite as well as finite dimensional separable Hilbert spaces ... but THE RESULTS are also intended for unbounded self-adjoint A", and then locates the extra analytic work precisely -- "concentrated in Theorem 5.2 and the Appendix to Section 6".  Section 8 is not on that list and has no counterpart there.  Third, Section 8 is itself scope-attentive where it means to be: parts (ii) and (iii) of Theorem 8.1 are explicitly restricted to finite dimensions, and part (ii) explicitly promises "natural infinite-dimensional extensions".  A section that qualifies its own parts and says nothing about unbounded operators is being read, not silently narrowed.
nonlocal_source_interpretation.alternative_literal_reading: Read "the hypotheses of the tan 2theta theorem" as importing that theorem at its widest certified scope, so that Theorem 8.1's iff and part (i) are claims about an unbounded self-adjoint A with bounded H.  Nothing in Section 8's printed text forbids this, the proof identities (8.1) and (8.2) are quadratic-form identities that survive an unbounded A, and the Theorem 8.2 homotopy A(sigma) = A + H - sigma H with a continuously varying spectral projector is meaningful for unbounded A and bounded H.  On this reading the registered bounded evidence is a proper specialization and these two rows are NARROW, exactly as the 2026-09-04 review classified them.  The repository does not claim this reading is wrong; it claims the bounded reading is the better-supported one, and records both so a reviewer can disagree with a specific argument rather than with silence.  The unbounded lift is tracked as live work in `GOAL.md`, and if it lands the question stops mattering.

separability.rule: Separability is a SOURCE-WIDE ambient convention (`scope_classification.category: source_wide_setup`), not a hypothesis of any counted result.  A canonical witness that does NOT assume `[TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H]` proves the printed result at every separable Hilbert space and at every non-separable one as well; that is a strict generalization on an ambient convention and is accepted as canonical evidence.  A canonical witness that DOES assume it is at the printed scope exactly.  Neither is a defect; what would be a defect is a witness assuming MORE than the ambient convention, and the one case that matters -- finite-dimensionality -- is refused separately by `S2-unbounded-scope.infinite-dimensional-scope.type_requirements.must_not_contain`.
separability.why_not_thin_separable_wrappers: The alternative is a thin wrapper per source-facing endpoint whose only content is an unused `[SeparableSpace]` binder.  That buys a name that looks like the paper and a theorem strictly weaker than the one proved, and it would have to be maintained on roughly forty endpoints.  The repository's rule about retaining printed hypotheses exists so that a hypothesis the paper's MATHEMATICS uses is not silently dropped.  Separability is not such a hypothesis for these estimates: every one of them is a Sylvester/gap argument that never invokes a countable dense set.  Where separability IS load-bearing -- the Hahn--Hellinger multiplicity invariants of Theorem 3.1, and the identification of the constructive crossed-defect condition with the source's Hilbert-dimension language -- the witnesses carry it, and this table records that.
